title: Agent tools: validate structural input (z.unknown/z.any) to prevent crash/corruption (generalize 1363)
description:
Systemic hardening of the agent command surface. Generalizes the 1363 crash: the
agent-protocol COMMAND_SCHEMAS accept several params as `z.unknown()` / `z.any()` /
loose `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`, so a malformed agent payload reaches a
document/timeline mutation with little/no validation -> crash (unguarded access, as
in 1363) or silent document corruption. This is the AGENT-TOOL-INPUT-VALIDATION theme
(cf 1350 collab untrusted-input validate/normalize; 1282 agent-chat tool policy).

PRIORITY: LOW-MED. The acute 1363 crash is already closed (doc_load now normalizes via
`ensureDocLibrary` at the handler). This task is systemic hardening, NOT an open crash.

=== 1363 PRECEDENT ===
doc_load took `document: z.unknown()` (packages/agent-protocol/src/index.ts:135-137)
and the handler blind-cast `pushDoc(document as FlashDocument)`. A library-less doc was
admitted into history.present and later crashed collab outbound `externalizeAssets`
(any reader doing `doc.library.items`). 1363 fixed the CRASH at the handler with
`ensureDocLibrary(document)` (packages/authoring-ui/src/agent/registry.ts:254-264,
called at :714) -- but the SCHEMA is still `z.unknown()`, and `ensureDocLibrary` only
backfills `library.items`: a doc missing `scenes`/`properties`/`history` invariants is
still admitted and can crash other readers. So the systemic gap remains.

=== JOB 1 AUDIT: agent tools taking unvalidated structural input (file:line) ===
All in packages/agent-protocol/src/index.ts unless noted. Handlers in
packages/authoring-ui/src/agent/registry.ts.

GENUINELY RISKY (structural input -> model mutation, little/no validation):

1. doc_load  `document: z.unknown()`  (index.ts:135-137; handler registry.ts:706-716)
   Failure mode: arbitrary object becomes the whole document. `ensureDocLibrary` only
   guarantees `library.items` is an array; a doc missing/malformed `scenes`,
   `properties`, layers, or frames is still pushed -> downstream crash (renderer,
   compiler, collab) or corruption. The schema does NO structural validation.

2. file_load_fla  `flaBase64: z.string()`  (index.ts:786-789; handler registry.ts:2148-2159)
   Failure mode: handler base64-decodes then `loadFla(bytes)` and `pushDoc(doc)` WITHOUT
   the `ensureDocLibrary` guard doc_load got. If loadFla produces a structurally-thin doc
   (or partially-parsed legacy FLA), the same library-less/invariant-less crash path as
   1363 is reachable here -- the 1363 fix was applied to doc_load ONLY, not this twin
   doc-replacement boundary. (The string schema is fine; the gap is the unguarded pushDoc.)

3. stage_update  `updates: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`  (index.ts:271-286;
   handler registry.ts:1094-1132)
   Failure mode: the `updates` bag is merged and cast straight into `updateDisplayObject`
   (`merged as Parameters<typeof updateDisplayObject>[4]`, registry.ts:1128). Only
   `instanceName` is validated; any other key/type (e.g. x/y/scale/rotation as a string or
   object, an unknown structural prop) is written onto the display object unchecked ->
   doc corruption / render or compile crash. `colorEffect` is `z.object({type}).passthrough()`
   (index.ts:279) -- effectively unvalidated beyond `type`.

4. timeline_set_tween  `props: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional()`
   (index.ts:425-431; handler registry.ts:1602)
   Failure mode: arbitrary tween props written to a keyframe with no field validation ->
   bad tween state, possible compile/interpolation crash.

LOWER RISK / NOTE:
5. jsfl_run  `source: z.string()`  (index.ts:739; handler registry.ts:2089) -- by design an
   escape hatch that runs arbitrary JSFL; out of scope for structural validation (its own
   sandbox/policy is the 1282 concern), but worth noting it is the broadest mutation surface.
6. selection_set / library_set_linkage / stage_place_instance -- structural but already use
   typed scalar/array fields; lower priority, verify no loose passthrough remains.

BENIGN (already validated / harmless): doc_get path (read-only), doc_set_properties
(typed positive numbers + string color), the *Result* schemas using z.unknown()/z.any()
(DocGetResult.value:67, SelectionGetResult.objects:347, JsflRunResult.returnValue:746,
FilterListResult.filters:855) -- these are OUTPUT shapes returned TO the model, not input,
so they cannot crash/corrupt the doc. scene_*/timeline frame ops use typed int indices.

=== RECOMMENDED FIX ===
Make structural agent inputs validate-or-normalize instead of trusting raw objects:
- doc_load: replace `document: z.unknown()` with a real (even if partial/lenient) Zod
  FlashDocument schema, OR broaden the handler normalization beyond `ensureDocLibrary`
  to assert/backfill ALL load-bearing invariants (scenes[], properties, each timeline's
  layers/frames) before pushDoc -- a malformed payload should yield a clear validation
  error or a safe normalized doc, never a crash.
- file_load_fla: route the loaded doc through the SAME normalization as doc_load
  (apply `ensureDocLibrary`/the broadened validator before pushDoc) so the 1363 fix
  covers BOTH doc-replacement boundaries.
- stage_update / timeline_set_tween: replace the `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`
  bags with a Zod schema enumerating the allowed display-object/tween fields and their
  types (x/y/scaleX/scaleY/rotation/alpha numbers, text string, blendMode enum, etc.),
  or validate/whitelist keys at the handler before the cast into updateDisplayObject.
- General principle: any COMMAND_SCHEMAS param that reaches a pushDoc/replaceDoc/
  updateDisplayObject/timeline/library mutation should be a real structural Zod schema
  (or handler-level validate+normalize), so a bad agent payload is rejected cleanly.

Theme: agent-tool-input-validation (cf 1350 collab inbound CRDT validate/normalize;
1282 agent-chat tool policy/confirmation; 1363 the doc_load crash this generalizes).
